description:
FILED s484d (2026-09-14).  t/op/tie.t produced NO rows until this session
(#1652: `run_multiple_progs('', \*DATA)` was its whole body and the helper was
a no-op).  It now runs all 95 of perl's rows: 14 pass, 81 fail.  63 of the 81
are `tie` itself announcing "not implemented" -- **#155**, already filed and
already the file's dominant fact.  THIS task is the other 18, classified from
the run's own kept artifacts (scratch/s484d/keep-cons/op_tie.t.out, one GOT
block per failing record):

   7  output differs and the tie mechanism RUNS -- so tie is not simply absent:
      records 15, 22, 30, 34, 35, 44, 70 get FETCH/STORE traces in the wrong
      order or with the wrong values ("STORE set 'BOBBINS'", "fetching... +
      123456", "00", "10101010").  These are the interesting ones: they say
      what a working tie gets wrong.
   2  the CHILD's SBCL compiler diagnostics land in the compared output --
      **#1773**, not a tie question at all.
   2  `Internals::SvREADONLY` announced and ignored, so there are no read-only
      scalars (docs/not-supported.md, "Perl's own internals").
   2  `Package PL- does not exist.` -- a tie class named by a lower-case
      one-letter package (`package l;`) reaches the runtime as `PL-`.
   2  `Blessing into '' is deprecated at unknown line 0.` -- perl's text is
      `Attempt to bless into a reference` / the deprecation with a real line;
      PCL's says "unknown line 0".
   2  `Can't use an undefined value as a symbol reference`.
   1  an undeclared BAREWORD in tie's argument slot: `tie(FH, ...)` emits a
      bare CL symbol read and dies "Undefined subroutine &main::FH" -- the
      same family as the s473t5d finding at the head of #1710.
   1  no GOT captured (row 60).

WHY IT IS ONE TASK: the rows all share one cause column value in
baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv (they share one TAP description, `[at
t/op/tie.t line 18]`, so the row baseline cannot attribute them
individually), and the clusters above are what that value points at.  Take
them in the order printed: the 7 "mechanism runs" rows are the only ones that
say something new about tie.
subject: op/tie.t's 18-row residue behind #155 -- eight clusters, five of them PCL bugs that have nothing to do with tie
